fields.description: Recipient's registration number. Accepts a regular GSTIN, a UN body UIN, a TDS deductor id, or a non-resident taxable person id. All four forms are 15 characters and carry the same check digit.
Trade name of the recipient. Not validated against the GSTIN.
Supplier's invoice number. Letters, digits, hyphen and slash only.
Invoice date. Accepted as D-MMM-YY, D-MMM-YYYY, DD-MMM-YY, DD-MMM-YYYY, or an Excel date serial (epoch 1899-12-30).
Total invoice value including tax. Non-negative, up to 13 integer digits and 2 decimals. Repeated on every rate row of the same invoice and must agree across them.

Place of supply as 'NN-Name'; only the numeric prefix is retained. Constrained by numeric range rather than by the state-code master, because the accepted range is wider than the list of live states — see notes.
Whether tax is payable by the recipient under reverse charge. Blank is treated as 'N'.
Proportion of the tax rate that applies. 65 covers the transitional real-estate rate; blank is treated as 100. Emitted as a factor (1.00 or 0.65) and applied to every computed tax amount.

Which of the four tables the invoice feeds: regular B2B (4A), SEZ with/without payment (6B), deemed export (6C), or intra-state supply attracting IGST. Matched on the import label after trimming, then reduced to its code.

Operator GSTIN for supplies made through an e-commerce operator. The column exists in the shared template but carries no value in this section — e-commerce supplies belong in the ECO tables. Any value rejects the row.
Combined tax rate for this line, in percent. One row per rate; an invoice spanning several rates spans several rows.
Taxable value at this rate, excluding tax. Non-negative, up to 11 integer digits and 2 decimals.
Cess payable on this line. Entered directly rather than derived from a rate; blank is treated as 0.

rules.description: An intra-state supply that nonetheless attracts IGST is only valid as a reverse-charge supply.
rules.message: Reverse Charge must be 'Y' when Invoice Type is 'Intra-State supplies attracting IGST'.

rules.description: Deemed exports are always forward-charge; tax is paid by the supplier.
rules.message: Reverse Charge must not be 'Y' when Invoice Type is 'Deemed Exp'.

rules.description: Reproduces the reference behavior: this section carries no e-commerce operator GSTIN at all.
rules.message: E-Commerce GSTIN must be blank in the B2B section; report supplies through an operator in the ECO tables.

keys.description: Proportion of the tax rate that applies, as a factor. The reference emits this key ONLY when it is 0.65 and discards every other value, so an unscaled row carries no such key at all. Verified against a file captured from the tool.
Code, not label: R, SEWP, SEWOP, DE, CBW.
Always empty in this section; whether the key is emitted at all is unconfirmed.
Integrated tax. Present on inter-state lines only.
Central tax. Present on intra-state lines only.
State/UT tax. Present on intra-state lines only, always equal to camt.

derivation_notes.gstr1.item_num: Line item number is derived from the rate, not a sequence: num = rt * 100 + 1. Rate 18 gives 1801, rate 0 gives 1. This is why the rate alone identifies a line within an invoice.
derivation_notes.gstr1.tax_split: A line is intra-state when the supplier's state code equals pos AND inv_typ is R or DE AND the supplier is not an SEZ unit; otherwise inter-state. Intra-state: camt = samt = round(txval * rt * 0.005 * diff_percent, 2). Inter-state: iamt = round(txval * rt * 0.01 * diff_percent, 2). Invoice type SEWOP (SEZ without payment of tax) forces every tax amount to 0 regardless of rate. Note the split turns on the supplier's own state, so the same row yields different output for different filers.
derivation_notes.gstr1.cess: csamt = round(Cess Amount, 2), or 0 when blank. Forced to 0 for invoice type SEWOP.

notes.text: Two rows sharing an invoice key and a rate do not sum — the later row silently replaces the earlier one. A workbook that splits one rate across two lines of the same invoice therefore under-reports, with no error raised. Reproduced deliberately for output equivalence; surfacing it as a warning is a candidate divergence.

Invoice numbers that are numerically zero ('0', '00', '0.0') are rejected even though they satisfy the character pattern, because the reference implementation compares Number(inum) != 0. Non-numeric numbers are unaffected.

Date parsing maps any unrecognized month abbreviation to December rather than failing, so a malformed month can silently land the invoice in the wrong month. The format check runs first and catches most such values; this only bites where the two disagree.

Place of supply is validated as a numeric range (01-38, 96, 97), not against the list of live states. The range is wider than the template's own dropdown, which offers 01-38 excluding 28 plus 97: validation therefore accepts 96 ('Other Country', absent from the dropdown) and also 28, which was merged into 37 and is no longer a live state code. Checking against the state-code master instead would reject 96, which the reference implementation accepts.

Whether the portal rejects place-of-supply code 28 is untested. Import accepts it, so a workbook carrying it passes validation here and may still fail on upload. Tightening to the dropdown list is a candidate divergence once the portal's behavior is known.

Invoice type labels differ between the Excel/CSV import path and the tool's own UI dropdown ('Deemed Exp' vs 'Deemed Exports', 'SEZ supplies with payment' vs 'SEZ Supplies with payment'). Import matches the labels recorded here; the masters file carries both.

The official section CSV shipped as a sample for this table no longer passes the tool's own import validation: 6 of its 15 rows carry an E-Commerce GSTIN, or pair 'Intra-State supplies attracting IGST' with Reverse Charge 'N'. The sample predates both rules. It is therefore usable as a layout reference but not as a positive test fixture.

Tax-rate-versus-supply-type validation is unreachable in the reference implementation — the routine returns true before any check runs — so rate/supply-type mismatches pass import. Whether the portal itself enforces the rule is untested, and no equivalent check is specified here.

The recipient's name is NOT sent to the portal. The reference strips cname from this section's envelope in removeCName() before writing the upload file, so the name is captured in the workbook for the filer's benefit only. Verified against a file captured from the tool.

The internal 'diffval' flag never reaches the upload JSON — the reference deletes it alongside the tax-rate factor. This resolves what was previously an open question. Verified against a file captured from the tool.
